title: Cosmic interactions
caption: Galaxy triplet NGC 7173, NGC 7174 and NGC 7176, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 7173, NGC 7174, NGC 7176 · constellation Piscis Austrinus · about 110 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Three galaxies share this frame, with NGC 7173 at the top, NGC 7174 at the bottom right and NGC 7176 at the bottom left. To some eyes, the combined shape of the lower pair resembles a sleeping baby. The trio lies about 106 million light-years away, in the direction of Piscis Austrinus, the Southern Fish, and belongs to one of the tight galaxy gatherings known as Hickson Compact Groups.

NGC 7173 and NGC 7176 are elliptical galaxies, smooth collections of stars without spiral arms. NGC 7174, by contrast, is a spiral. Its dust lanes look badly disturbed, and it trails a long, twisted tail.

That disturbance seems to show that the two lower galaxies are interacting right now, their gravity pulling each other out of shape. Astronomers have suggested that all three galaxies will eventually merge into one.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.44 x 5.54 arcminutes) and distance (110 million light years), the frame spans roughly 206,000 × 177,000 light-years. Its light set out about 110 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a visible-light image made with the FORS1 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope through three filters, B, V and R. The colour assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The long telescope exposure collects far more light than the eye, helping to bring out faint features such as the twisted tail and dust lanes.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image covers an area of sky about 5.3 arcminutes across. It was assembled from data taken with the FORS1 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, pulled from the ESO Science Archive, then processed by ESO's Henri Boffin.
alt: Three galaxies against a dark sky, one at the top and two at the bottom, one of them with a long twisted tail.
